prompt:
PLAN 02 — THE FIRST LINE | THE VOICE ARRIVES

Create a 15-second cinematic sequence for Seedance 2.5.
Horizontal 16:9.
Exactly three shots lasting four, four and seven seconds.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:
Young Homayoun = {{CHAR_HOMAYOUN_YOUNG}}
Composer = {{CHAR_COMPOSER}}
Father = {{CHAR_FATHER}}

LOCATION REFERENCE:
Early-2000s recording studio, vocal booth and connected control room = {{LOC_RECORDING_STUDIO}}

PROP REFERENCES:
Mixing console = {{PROP_MIXING_CONSOLE}}
Studio microphone and pop filter = {{PROP_MIC}}
Studio headphones = {{PROP_HEADPHONES}}
Lyric sheet = {{PROP_LYRIC_SHEET}}

AUDIO REFERENCE: 
Original vocal performance of “می‌تراود مهتاب” = {{AUDIO_MITARAVAD_MAHTAB}} 

Preserve the exact character appearance, studio geography, wardrobe, microphone placement, headphone design, lighting direction and blocking established in PLAN 01.

CONTINUITY START STATE:

Direct continuation from PLAN 01.

Homayoun remains inside the vocal booth facing the studio glass.

The studio headphones remain firmly over both ears and stay there for the entire plan.

The lyric sheet remains in his hand.

The composer remains seated behind the mixing console inside the control room.

The father remains standing separately in the control room.

Homayoun now turns inward toward the act of singing.

SPATIAL LOCK:

Whenever the glass and control room are visible from the booth, Homayoun must be facing them, with his back or back-three-quarter orientation toward camera.

Whenever Homayoun is viewed from the front, the background behind him must be the booth wall, never the glass.

FINAL SHOT RULE:

The final shot of the entire 30-second sequence must be Homayoun singing. Do not cut away after he begins singing. Do not add a final mixer shot, reaction shot, or control-room insert after the singing starts.

SHOT 02A | 00:15–00:19 | THE TURN INWARD

Begin with a 65mm over-the-shoulder view from behind Homayoun inside the booth.

Because the glass is visible, Homayoun faces the glass and control room.

His headphones remain fully on his ears.

He holds the lyric sheet lower now, becoming still after receiving the composer’s cue and his father’s nod.

His breathing settles.

The composer remains partially obscured in his separate position behind the console.

The father remains separately visible elsewhere in the control room.

Homayoun’s body quiets as he prepares to sing.

SHOT 02B | 00:19–00:23 | READY TO BEGIN

Cut to a 50mm frontal medium-close shot of Homayoun at eye level.

Because this is a frontal view, the background behind him is the booth’s interior wall and acoustic treatment only.

The headphones remain clearly visible over both ears.

The microphone and pop filter are positioned naturally in front of him without hiding his face completely.

He steadies the lyric sheet, lets one calm breath settle, and gently parts his lips.

The camera begins a slow, smooth forward move.

SHOT 02C | 00:23–00:30 | “می‌تراود مهتاب”

Continue the same frontal camera axis into a closer framing over seven seconds.

Keep the booth wall behind Homayoun, never the glass.

Using the supplied vocal recording as the exact performance source, Homayoun begins singing “می‌تراود مهتاب”.

Perform precise lip-sync to the supplied recording, matching the exact mouth shapes, Persian phoneme articulation, breath timing and phrasing.

The opening “می...” emerges softly and naturally.

As the phrase continues, his face opens almost imperceptibly and his presence deepens.

The emotional transition is from concentrated readiness into quiet certainty.

Maintain Homayoun as the uninterrupted emotional center.

Do not cut away to the mixer, VU meter, composer, father, or any other insert.

End while he is still singing.

PERFORMANCE AND LIP-SYNC:

The supplied vocal recording is the absolute timing reference for Homayoun’s performance.

Preserve natural facial anatomy.

Lip articulation follows the exact Persian phonemes of the supplied performance.

Facial movement remains subtle and physically realistic.

The emotional change happens gradually through breath, focus, eyes and posture.

COMPOSER VISIBILITY:

The composer is never presented in a clean hero portrait.

Whenever visible, use console hardware, foreground objects, studio-glass reflections, three-quarter orientation, partial silhouette and controlled shallow focus to limit facial detail.

LIGHT AND IMAGE:

Continue the same warm practical lighting from PLAN 01.

Soft highlights on microphone metal, headphone material and booth surfaces.

Natural exposure and restrained contrast.

The final singing shot becomes progressively more intimate as the camera approaches.

Keep the visual texture tactile, human and understated.

SOUND:

The supplied vocal recording enters during SHOT 02C and remains the dominant sound through the end.

Subtle studio room tone continues underneath.

A small breath detail precedes the first syllable.

Gentle electrical hum remains low beneath the voice.

ADDITIONAL MUSIC: none.
ADDITIONAL DIALOGUE: none.
